report.source_text: Two weeks prior to this hospital admission, she developed a fever, cough and back pain amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. The patient tested positive for COVID-19 and was treated with azithromycin for 5 days at home. Subsequently, over the next 2 weeks, her fever and cough resolved, but the lower back pain persisted. This was characterised by a throbbing, 7/10 intensity (numeric rating scale), radiating to both the lower extremities. She then had a new onset of numbness, pins and needles sensation in the left lower extremity associated with mild weakness. These same symptoms then progressed to the contralateral lower extremity over the next 24 hours with an unstable gait. This progression triggered an emergency room visit. She had no headaches, loss of consciousness, changes in mental status, changes in vision and speech, difficulty swallowing, seizure-like symptoms or urine/bowel incontinence.

clinician.trajectory_summary: 58-year-old woman with recent COVID-19 infection (2 weeks prior, confirmed positive) presented with progressive lower extremity paresthesias and weakness. Initial presentation included fever, cough, and back pain that resolved, but back pain persisted. She then developed numbness and pins-and-needles sensation in the left lower extremity with mild weakness, progressing to the contralateral lower extremity within 24 hours with unstable gait, prompting ER visit. Initial admission exam showed normal motor strength (5/5 all extremities) and normal deep tendon reflexes bilaterally, with no sensory level or upper motor neuron findings. Within 24 hours of admission, she developed worsening ascending weakness (3/5 bilateral lower extremities, 4/5 left upper extremity) with diminished deep tendon reflexes compared to admission. Lumbar puncture revealed albumin-cytologic dissociation (WBC 2 cu/mm, protein 117 mg/dL) consistent with GBS. MRI lumbar spine ruled out structural myelopathy, showing only neural foraminal narrowing with unremarkable conus medullaris. She was treated with IVIG 2 mg/kg for 4 days with respiratory monitoring and gabapentin for neuropathic pain. After treatment, her symptoms improved significantly and she was discharged to acute rehabilitation for physical therapy.
